content: 1. Rifapentine significantly reduces the levels of darunavir by enhancing its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Alternative medications should be considered to avoid this interaction. 2. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used, or close monitoring is required. 3. Darunavir increases the levels of rifaximin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 4. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Cobicistat also increases rimegepant levels via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 5. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of riociguat by reducing its metabolism through CYP3A4. Cobicistat also increases riociguat levels via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Monitor for signs of hypotension and adjust the riociguat dose as needed. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite, DP-5439, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of risperidone through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be necessary. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Darunavir and ritonavir together increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Ritonavir also increases darunavir levels via CYP3A4. Alternative drugs should be considered. 9. Darunavir increases the levels of rivaroxaban by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect. Avoid coadministration due to the increased risk of bleeding. If unavoidable, monitor closely. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of roflumilast (both systemic and topical) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided if possible. 12. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ropivacaine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Darunavir decreases the effects of rosiglitazone through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 14. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of rosuvastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, the dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. 15. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of cobicistat and darunavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 16. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib (both systemic and topical) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg BID with platelet counts ≥100 x 10^9/L. Avoid use with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. 18. Darunavir increases the levels of salmeterol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of cardiovascular effects, including QT prolongation, palpitations, and sinus tachycardia. 19. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministered, limit saxagliptin to 5 mg/day. 20. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of seladelpar by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect. Monitor for adverse effects if coadministered with BCRP inhibitors. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of selexipag by affecting ABCG2 (BCRP) transport. Monitor for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the selpercatinib dose and monitor for side effects. 23. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dosage and resume the original dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 24. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of sertraline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect. Carefully titrate the SSRI dose based on clinical assessment. Darunavir may also decrease sertraline levels through an unspecified mechanism. 25. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated when sildenafil is used chronically for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). If used for erectile dysfunction, do not exceed 25 mg every 48 hours. 26. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of silodosin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of simvastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of rhabdomyolysis. 28. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of siponimod by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors plus moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 29. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 30. Darunavir decreases the effects of sitagliptin through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 31. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of sofpironium topical by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 32. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 33. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat has a similar effect. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 34. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of sorafenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Darunavir and sparsentan may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming. 36. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of therapeutic failure and resistance development. 37. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of stiripentol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. 38. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely.
